text: Visitors have raised concerns about the timed-entry ticketing system, with several reporting frustration over sold-out tickets and lack of walk-up options, which has limited access for some. Parking and traffic flow around the site were frequently mentioned as problematic, including narrow lanes and insufficient camper parking. Some reviews criticized the heavy use of AI in exhibits and questioned the overall interpretation and presentation of Theodore Roosevelt’s legacy. While many appreciated the building’s architecture and interactive exhibits, issues with crowding, ticket pricing, and amenities like restrooms and the café were noted. These points suggest areas where visitor experience could be improved.

windows.7: Over the past week, several visitors expressed frustration with the timed-entry ticketing system, noting that tickets sell out quickly and there are no options for walk-up admission, which has led to some guests being turned away after long travel. Parking and traffic flow around the site were also criticized for being poorly designed, with narrow lanes and minimal camper parking. Some reviews mentioned long lines at security and a lack of communication about parking and ticket availability. A few visitors questioned the value of the admission price compared to other presidential libraries and raised concerns about the heavy use of AI in exhibits, feeling it detracts from the experience. Despite these issues, many found the architecture and interactive exhibits to be positive aspects.
